plan: - Satellite transceiver module (e.g., Iridium, Globalstar) for long-range communication. - High-capacity lithium-ion battery pack and power management circuitry for extended operation. - Microcontroller (e.g., STM32, ESP32) for UI, audio processing, and module control. - Audio codec, microphone, speaker, and OLED display for user interaction. - Custom PCB design for component integration and robust signal integrity. - Durable, weather-resistant enclosure with integrated satellite antenna mount.

nodes.name: Iridium Satellite Transceiver
nodes.description: Iridium SBD modem for global command, control, and telemetry communication.

nodes.name: Main Microcontroller
nodes.description: High-performance SoC with integrated Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, serving as the main controller for the watch.

nodes.name: Li-ion Battery Charger
nodes.description: Li-Ion battery charger with power path management for single-cell battery.

nodes.name: Power Management IC (PMIC)
nodes.description: High-efficiency buck-boost converter for 3.3V digital logic.

nodes.name: Audio Codec
nodes.description: High-performance multi-channel audio codec for digital input and 4-channel analog output.

nodes.name: Miniature Speaker
nodes.description: Small, general-purpose speaker for audio output.

nodes.name: OLED Display
nodes.description: Small OLED display for system status and feedback. Located on the handheld head.

nodes.name: Main Enclosure (Front Shell)
nodes.description: Ergonomic front shell of the walkie-talkie enclosure, designed for grip and housing the display and controls.

nodes.name: Main Enclosure (Rear Shell)
nodes.description: Rear shell of the walkie-talkie enclosure, designed for battery compartment and satellite antenna mounting point.

nodes.name: Enclosure Sealing Gasket
nodes.description: Custom-cut silicone gasket for weather-sealing the main enclosure halves against water and dust ingress.

nodes.name: Main PCB Mounting Plate
nodes.description: Internal structural plate to securely mount the custom PCB within the enclosure.

nodes.name: Iridium Module Mount
nodes.description: Custom bracket to securely mount the Iridium satellite transceiver module to the main PCB mounting plate.

nodes.name: Li-ion Battery Pack Holder
nodes.description: Custom holder designed to securely cradle the high-capacity Li-ion battery pack within the enclosure, preventing movement.

nodes.name: OLED Display Bezel
nodes.description: Bezel to secure and frame the OLED display within the front enclosure, providing a clean appearance.

nodes.name: Speaker Grille
nodes.description: Protective grille for the miniature speaker, integrated into the front enclosure for sound output.

nodes.name: Microphone Mount
nodes.description: Small mount to position and secure the MEMS microphone optimally in the enclosure.

nodes.name: Satellite Antenna Mount Adapter
nodes.description: Rugged adapter for securely attaching an external Iridium satellite antenna to the rear of the enclosure.

nodes.name: M3 Button Head Screws
nodes.description: Fasteners for securing the enclosure halves, internal PCB, and mounting brackets.
nodes.productName: M3x10mm Button Head Socket Cap Screws

nodes.name: M3 Heat-Set Inserts
nodes.description: Brass inserts to provide robust threaded points for M3 screws in 3D-printed parts.
nodes.productName: M3 Brass Threaded Heat Set Inserts

nodes.name: Tactile Buttons (Set)
nodes.description: Rugged, waterproof tactile push buttons for user input (PTT, menu navigation).

nodes.name: Main Microcontroller Mount
nodes.description: Standoff bracket sized to the Main Microcontroller's mounting hole pattern. M2.5 holes for board fasteners; vented underside for airflow.

nodes.name: Audio Codec Mount
nodes.description: Adapter plate for the Audio Codec that bolts to the main chassis with M3 hardware. Includes wire-routing channels.

subSteps.title: 3D Print all mechanical enclosure and mounting components
Install M3 heat-set inserts into PCB mounting plate and main enclosure rear
Clean and deburr all 3D printed parts, test-fit main enclosure halves
Test fit the OLED display, speaker, microphone, and tactile buttons into the front enclosure
Prepare and tin wire leads for all electrical components
Solder power management IC, Li-ion charger, and Li-ion battery pack power connections
Solder all power (VCC/VDD, GND) connections from PMIC to main MCU, Iridium module, audio codec, microphone, and OLED display
Solder UART connections between main MCU and Iridium module
Solder I2S/PDM audio connections between main MCU, audio codec, microphone, and speaker
Solder I2C and GPIO control connections between main MCU, OLED display, and Li-ion charger
Perform continuity checks on all soldered power and data lines to prevent short circuits
Connect main MCU to computer via programming interface and flash initial firmware
Apply power (via charger USB or battery) and verify stable voltage rails (3.3V) at all power consumers
Test I2C communication with OLED display, audio codec, and Li-ion charger
Verify UART communication with Iridium Satellite Transceiver module
Test audio path: record from microphone and play sound through speaker via audio codec
Verify Li-ion charger functionality and battery status reporting
Perform basic functional test of Iridium module (e.g., network registration check)
Mount the Main Microcontroller onto its mount, and the Audio Codec onto its mount
Mount the Iridium SBD Module into its mount and the Li-ion Battery Pack into its holder
Secure all mounted components (MCU, Audio Codec, Iridium Module, Battery Holder) onto the PCB mounting plate using M3 screws
Mount the PCB mounting plate assembly into the Main Enclosure Rear using M3 screws
Install OLED Display into its bezel, Microphone into its mount, and Speaker into its grille, then secure these into the Main Enclosure Front
Route all internal wires neatly, ensuring strain relief and avoiding interference with moving parts or enclosure closing
Place the enclosure sealing gasket, then carefully close the Main Enclosure Front and Rear shells using M3 screws
Mount the Satellite Antenna Mount Adapter to the Main Enclosure Rear

tools: Heat-set insert soldering tip or specialized tool
USB-to-UART converter (if main_mcu lacks onboard debugger)
assumptions: Basic soldering and electronics assembly experience
Familiarity with microcontroller firmware development (e.g., Arduino IDE, PlatformIO, or vendor-specific toolchain)
Understanding of I2C, UART, and SPI communication protocols
Access to a computer for firmware flashing and testing
A stable 5V USB power supply for charging and initial testing
